title: Token-Level LLM Collaboration via FusionRoute
text: our FusionRoute enables effective collaboration among multiple models by (a) selecting the most domain-appropriate models for accurate specialized responses and (b) delivering consistently high-quality outputs on general datasets. We compare FusionRoute against a broad set of baselines including sequence-level collaboration, token-level collaboration, model merging, and single-model fine-tuning. For sequence-level collaboration, we compare with the common Sequence Selection, where each expert independently generates a full response using greedy decoding and an external reward model selects the highest-scoring output. For the token-level collaboration, we include Collab (Chakraborty et al., 2025 ) , which performs controlled decoding by evaluating candidate tokens from multiple models using an external reward signal; we follow the original decoding procedure and replace only the reward model when necessary to ensure fair comparison across model families. To evaluate training-free expert integration, we include two popular model merging approaches, DARE (Yu et al., 2024 ) and TaskArithmetic (Ilharco et al., 2022 ) . We additionally include a Fine-tuned Model baseline obtained by directly fine-tuning the base LLM using the same SFT and DPO procedures as FusionRoute , but without any routing or collaboration mechanism, thereby isolating the benefit of token-level multi-LLM collaboration and complementary logit contributions. We conduct experiments on both the Llama-3 (Dubey et al., 2024 ) and Gemma-2 (Team et al., 2024 ) families, using the model checkpoints provided by He et al. ( 2025 ) .
